title: fix(tooling): the lucide gate names the seam in `data-table`, and judges its own `resolver` field
body:
Fixes #7492

## What was wrong

`RECORD_READING_TYPES['data-table']` in `scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` declared its
`resolver` as `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx`. That module does not read
lucide's runtime `icons` record.

Re-verified on today's tree (branched from `900f8d995`), all three of the card's readings still hold:

- `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx:12` — `import { resolveIcon } from '../action/resolve-icon';`
- `:401` — `const ActionIcon = resolveIcon(action.icon);`
- it is **absent** from part 1's discovered record-reader set, which on this tree is exactly one entry,
  `packages/components/src/renderers/action/resolve-icon.ts` (read off `--report`).

So it is a router, and it was the only routed entry not spelled in the two-part form its six siblings
use — RECORD-READER, then the renderer in a parenthesised `(via ...)` tail. (Placeholders spelled as
words on purpose: GitHub deletes angle-bracket-shaped tokens from a stored body, code spans and fences
included.)

## The change, in two commits

**1. The one entry** — `a310e59f9`. `data-table` now reads
`packages/components/src/renderers/action/resolve-icon.ts (via renderers/complex/data-table.tsx)`,
copied from the shape the six siblings pin. No other entry and no other field was touched; the table is
now internally consistent, which the card noted would be the effect.

**2. The thing worth more than the string** — `a591823c6`. Nothing validated `resolver` at all: it
could name a module with no lookup in it, or a file that does not exist, and this gate stayed green.
That is a declaration naming a module which does not do the declared thing — the class the gate exists
to end, one level up in its own tooling. `censusResolverProblems` closes it in two halves, neither of
which invents a vocabulary:

1. the part before the `(via ...)` tail must be one of the record-reading resolvers **part 1
   rediscovers from source on every run**, so a router's own file can only appear inside the tail —
   which is what makes the two-part form the one shape a routed entry can take. Existence comes with
   it: part 1 already fails on a declared reader it cannot rediscover.
2. the path inside the tail must resolve to a file that exists under one of the **ancestor directories
   of that reader** (`renderers/form/button.tsx` against `packages/components/src/`,
   `plugin-view/src/ViewSwitcher.tsx` against `packages/`) — so the roots to try are read off the
   reader rather than listed here. A renamed or moved renderer otherwise leaves a string that reads
   perfectly and points nowhere.

`analyze`'s `recordReadingTypes` / `declaredRecordReaders` overrides are deliberately **not** forwarded
to it: it judges the declarations this file ships, exactly as `selfTest()` judges the lucide install
rather than the tree under analysis.

## Evidence

### The string change moves no verdict

`resolver` is printed as `Resolved through: ...` beside a violation and is a predicate for nothing, so
this is the whole acceptance reading:

- `node scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs --report` — stdout **byte-identical** before and
  after (`diff` exit 0), exit 0 both times. The same holds with commit 2 applied.
- Because a green run never prints the string, it was also exercised where it does appear: `analyze`
  run over a throwaway fixture tree holding one `data-table` node with the retired spelling `edit`,
  under the old and the new declaration. Same verdict both times (0 errors, 1 violation, same site,
  same detail) and **exactly one differing line**:

```
-       Resolved through: packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx
+       Resolved through: packages/components/src/renderers/action/resolve-icon.ts (via renderers/complex/data-table.tsx)
```

### The pin is green on the existing entries, and red in both directions

- Green over all **14** shipped entries, 9 of which carry the `(via ...)` tail — so the two-part form
  is actually exercised rather than merely permitted. The five `action:*` entries name the seam
  directly and stay green: the rule is "name the module whose lookup the names reach", not "use
  parentheses".
- **Ablation.** Re-introduced the pre-repair one-part spelling on the committed tree, proved the
  mutation landed on disk (blob hash `3d38830` to `5461123`; anchor counts flipped, new 1 to 0 and old
  0 to 1), then ran the gate: **exit 1**, and the only failure line is the pin naming itself and the
  entry:

```
    - census entry `data-table` declares resolver `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx`,
      which is NOT one of the record-reading resolvers part 1 discovered
      (packages/components/src/renderers/action/resolve-icon.ts). ... See objectui#7492.
```

  Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH` under a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`, and the
  restoration proven **by state**: worktree blob hash back to the HEAD blob `3d38830`, anchor counts
  back to 1/0, `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty.
- The two other directions are pinned as unit rows rather than by ablation: a `(via ...)` tail naming a
  renamed renderer, and a malformed shape.

### Suite

`pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/check-lucide-icon-record-names.test.ts` — **42 passed** before,
**42 passed** with commit 1 alone, **48 passed** with commit 2 (six new rows, section 8). Under the
ablation it is 13 failed / 35 passed.

⚠️ Worth knowing at review time: because the check is a self-test of the shipped declarations rather
than of the analysed tree, a bad declaration reds **every** fixture row that asserts an empty `errors`
list, not only section 8. That is the existing behaviour of `selfTest()` (a broken lucide install reds
the same rows) and it fails loudly rather than quietly, but it is a real coupling and it is deliberate.

### Gates run locally, on the final commit `a591823c6`

| command | verdict |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs --report` | exit 0, output byte-identical to the pre-change baseline |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/check-lucide-icon-record-names.test.ts` | 48 passed |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — `✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | exit 0 — `✅  check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 6360 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `node scripts/check-entry-guard.mjs --self-test` | exit 0 — 63 cases pass |
| `node scripts/check-entry-guard.mjs` | exit 0 — 66 scripts/ files, 60 export bindings, 60 inert on import |
| `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec eslint` on the two changed files | exit 0 |

Every exit code was captured by redirecting first, never through a pipe.

### Not run, stated plainly

The repo-wide `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint`, and the rest of the `check:*` farm — CI runs that farm
exactly once anyway. The narrowing is declared rather than silent: the two changed files are
`scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` and its own pin suite, the module has **no importers**
outside that suite (the two other files mentioning it by name do so in comments only, verified), and
`scripts/**` is not a governed surface.

## Two notes for the reviewer

1. The triage comment's boundary 1 said that changing line 391 alone would turn
   `scripts/__tests__/check-lucide-icon-record-names.test.ts` red. On today's tree it does not: the
   string `data-table` does not occur anywhere in that suite (the by-exact-string rows are `button` and
   `icon`), and the suite is 42/42 green with commit 1 alone. Commit 2 is what puts a test row on this
   entry.
2. The card's premise held in full — `resolver` is diagnostic, no verdict moved, and nothing went from
   unjudged to judged by commit 1. Commit 2 deliberately makes the field load-bearing for the gate's
   own self-check, which is the invited follow-up, not a falsification of the premise.
